newsitem.title: USA: Figgie says contract will help unit's sales.
newsitem.headline: Figgie says contract will help unit's sales.

text.p: Figgie International Inc expects a new contract with Litton Industries Inc to help Figgie's Interstate Electronics unit's sales by about $40 million over five years including $2-$5 million in late 1997, chairman Jack Reilly said in a conference call Friday.

Interstate Wednesday was awarded a contract to supply GPS (global positioning satellite) flight management systems to retrofit commercial aircraft now equipped with Litton inertial navigation systems, he said.
Interstate accounted for $90.5 million of Figgie's 1996 $385.7 million sales. It makes guidance and navigation systems and is trying to sell military systems commercially.
"It will always have a core military business but its growth potential is in the commercial side," Reilly said in a telephone interview after the conference call.

"It's been really frustrating that we have not got some of the new (Interstate) businesses off and aggressively running," he said, adding that Figgie believes the new contract "bodes well for increased commercial GPS sales in the second half of 1997."
The unit had a fourth quarter operating loss of $29,000 on net sales of $21.8 million and for the year had an operating profit of $5.1 million on the $90.5 million sales.

Figgie's Scott unit, which makes fire and aviation oxygen equipment, had $7.4 million fourth quarter operating profits on sales of $36.0 million. For the year, operating profits were $26.9 million on sales of $136.7 million.
Reilly said Scott will likely make "a couple" of acquisitions in 1997, each in the $10-$15 million range.

Its Snorkel unit makes aerial work platforms and had fourth quarter operating profits of $4.0 million on $34.4 million sales. For the year, operating profits were $22.1 million on sales of $158.5 million.
Reilly said Snorkel fourth quarter sales were hurt by delays in shipping some units due to supplier parts shortages and by customer perceptions the unit might still be for sale.

In July Figgie said it would pursue sale of one or more business units, but in October said it had decided to keep Snorkel, Scott and Interstate and sell only Taylor, which makes thermometers. That was completed in December.
Snorkel had strong business bookings and a normalized backlog in December, Reilly said.
As reported, Reilly, 53, resigned Friday as president and chief executive officer but will remain as a non-employee chairman. He becomes chief executive of Stant Corp.
Figgie has sold 17 units since 1994. Reilly arrived two years ago to oversee a restructuring and turnaround.

"I would like to convey to our shareholders that I am very, very optimistic about the future of this company," he said, adding he is returning to the Chicago area for personal and family reasons. "This is not the rat deserting the ship. This ship is in very, very good shape."
As reported, fourth quarter net income including discontinued operations was $0.33 a share on sales of $92.2 million versus a year-ago net loss of $0.17 a share on $87.7 million sales.
For 1996 Figgie earned $1.25 a share on $385.7 million sales versus a loss of $0.89 on $340.8 million sales.
